Timeline::month_scalar¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

int Timeline::month_scalar() const

Read One Calendar Month¶

month_scalar() returns the scalar instant’s local calendar month as an ordinary integer from 1 through 12. It is the scalar counterpart of month(): choose this method when C++ code needs one value, and choose month() when rank and shape must be preserved in a Series.

Month extraction uses the Timeline’s timezone. It does not divide epoch time into fixed-duration blocks because calendar months have unequal lengths and local midnight does not necessarily align with UTC midnight. A timezone conversion near a month boundary can therefore change the result.

Example: Leap-Day Month¶

const auto leap_day = pluss::timeline::make("2024-02-29T23:45:00Z");
std::cout << "month=" << leap_day.month_scalar() << '\n';

Output¶

month=2

Example: Timezone Crossing A Month Boundary¶

const auto utc = pluss::timeline::make("2025-01-01T01:30:00Z");
const auto edmonton = utc.tz_convert("America/Edmonton");
std::cout << "UTC=" << utc.month_scalar() << '\n'
          << "Edmonton=" << edmonton.month_scalar() << '\n';

Output¶

UTC=1
Edmonton=12

Example: Absence¶

const auto nat = pluss::timeline::make("");
std::cout << nat.month_scalar() << '\n';

Output¶

-1

The absent sentinel lies outside the valid 1..12 range. A one-element vector is not accepted; call month() for vector, matrix, or higher-rank values.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • The return value is one-based; January is 1, not 0.

  • The receiver must be rank zero, not merely contain one element.

  • NaT returns -1 rather than throwing.

  • Timezone conversion can change the month while preserving the instant.

  • The operation is read-only and leaves all original precision intact.

See Also¶

  • month(): shape-preserving extraction.

  • month_name(): textual month labels.

  • quarter_scalar(): the enclosing quarter as a scalar field.
